column1: # INDEX-spread.tsv — one row per preserved pinned8 SPREAD-form archive, the arm that
# closes this era's both-arms condition. A second index rather than rows appended to
# INDEX.tsv, because that file is frozen at the 24 confined archives and says so; an
# unindexed set beside an indexed one is the enumeration gap this file removes.
# Membership is the MEASURED predicate, as next door: an archive is spread-form because
# it CARRIES a `doms=`/`nodedoms=` field, never because of its revision or its name. The
# confined arm self-identifies by lacking that field, so the two indexes partition the
# directory by what the artifacts record and the complement of each checks the other.
# `kind` uses INDEX.tsv's own vocabulary: `ladder` is a judged sweep (BenchmarkScale plus
# the ceiling arm), `clock-window` is a Peak-only log from the same run. Both arms
# preserve both kinds, which is what lets them be enumerated on the same terms.
# columns 1-10 are INDEX.tsv's, so the two indexes read the same way. Added here:
#  11 pin_doms    the cache domain of every masked core (§5 rule 5's spread invariant)
#  12 nodedoms    how many domains the node offered, so the mask's shape is checkable
#  13 instrument  the ceiling instrument version the row was measured by (§5 rule 18)
